name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East for its pine-covered hills, pleasant climate, colonial architecture, and vibrant Khasi culture. Major educational and tourism hub.
facts: Named after U Lei Shillong deity

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, located near Laitkor about 10 km from Shillong city. Offers panoramic views of the Shillong plateau, city, and surrounding hills; popular for sunrise and sunset.
facts: Sacred site for U Lei Shillong
Restricted area near Air Force base; ID required

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall in Upper Shillong about 12 km from the city centre. Locally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew; named for a former elephant-shaped rock. Popular picnic and short-visit spot amid pine forests.
facts: Named after an elephant-shaped rock destroyed by earthquake

name: Ward's Lake (Nan Polok)
description: Artificial horseshoe-shaped lake in central Shillong, also called Pollock Lake or Nan Polok. Built in 1894, surrounded by botanical gardens, cobblestone paths, a wooden bridge, and boating facilities; one of the city's most visited spots.
facts: Local name Nan Polok or Pollock Lake

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures (Museum)
description: Seven-storey museum in Mawlai, Shillong showcasing the indigenous cultures of Northeast India's eight states through galleries of artefacts, textiles, musical instruments, and traditional life. Opened for public viewing around 2010; major cultural attraction.
facts: Focus on tribal cultures of Northeast India

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Famous plateau town in East Khasi Hills, formerly known as Cherrapunji, renowned for extremely high rainfall and dramatic waterfalls. Base for exploring Nohkalikai, Mawsmai Cave, root bridges, and deep gorges on the southern slopes.
facts: One of the wettest places on Earth
Gateway to Nohkalikai and living root bridges

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: India’s tallest plunge waterfall at approximately 340 m, dropping from the Sohra plateau into a turquoise pool. Named after a local legend of Ka Likai; dramatic viewpoint on the cliff edge amid misty forests.

name: Mawsmai Cave (Krem Mawsmai)
description: Accessible limestone show cave near Sohra with illuminated stalactites, stalagmites, and passages. One of the first developed caves in Meghalaya; short walk through decorated chambers.
facts: Name means Oath Stone Cave in Khasi

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented waterfall near Sohra that splits into seven streams during monsoon, cascading over the cliff into the valley. Dramatic multi-stream fall visible from viewpoints.
facts: Splits into seven streams in heavy rain

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, grown from rubber fig roots over decades by Khasi communities. Reached by a steep descent of about 3,000–3,500 stone steps from Tyrna; major adventure and cultural attraction.

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Widely known as Asia’s cleanest village, a Khasi settlement near the Bangladesh border with bamboo walkways, living root bridge at nearby Riwai, and community-managed eco-tourism. Neat houses, orchid gardens, and strict cleanliness rules.
facts: Single living root bridge nearby at Riwai

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic cliff-edge viewpoint and canyon about 25 km from Shillong near Smit. Offers sweeping views into deep green gorges; steep steps lead down toward Rasong village. Popular for sunrise, photography, and short treks.
facts: Steep descent to valley villages possible

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest (Law Lyngdoh)
description: Ancient sacred grove protected by Khasi tradition near Mawphlang village, about 25 km from Shillong. Nothing may be removed from the forest; home to old-growth trees, monoliths, and rich biodiversity. Guided walks only.
facts: Protected by traditional Khasi beliefs for centuries
No removal of anything from the forest
